opus-5.5.text:
Honestly, I think the dream is something that can take on the kind of work that's really tedious but still requires judgment. In my personal life, that's things like planning a trip end to end: not just finding flights, but comparing options against what I actually care about, booking everything, dealing with the reservations, and coming back to me only when there's a real decision to make. Or the admin stuff that piles up, like returns, appointments, paperwork, figuring out an insurance claim. Each of those is maybe twenty minutes of annoying back-and-forth, and they add up.

At work, it's similar but at a bigger scale. A lot of what I do involves gathering information from a bunch of different places: reading through docs, pulling data, synthesizing what's out there on a topic, and then turning it into something useful like a report, a spreadsheet, or a first draft. If an agent could do the research and the assembly, I could spend my time on the parts where I actually add something, like deciding what matters and what to do next.

I think the important thing is that it should feel less like a tool you operate and more like a capable collaborator you delegate to. You give it a goal, it figures out the steps, it uses whatever it needs (a browser, a terminal, your files), and it knows when to check in with you. That last part matters a lot. Trust comes from the agent being good at knowing what it shouldn't do without asking, like spending money or sending something on your behalf.

And over time I'd hope it learns your preferences, so you don't have to re-explain everything each time. The more context it has about you, the more it can just handle things the way you would have.

r001.rationale: The candidate describes one general agent handling personal tasks such as trip planning and work tasks such as research and drafting.

r002.rationale: The candidate says nothing about AI models improving quickly or surprising most people.

fable-5.1.text:
Thanks for having me. I think the honest answer is that I want it to take over the stuff I keep putting off because it's tedious, not because it's hard.

At work, that means something like: I describe a question I have, and the agent goes and does the research, pulls together the sources, reads them carefully, and comes back with a real synthesis I can actually trust, with citations I can check. Not a summary of the first three search results, but the kind of thing a good analyst would hand you after a few hours. And then it keeps going. If I say "actually, now compare that to what we were doing last quarter," it should already have the context and just do it.

In my personal life it's more mundane but honestly maybe more valuable. Planning a trip end to end: knowing my preferences, finding flights, booking the hotel that's near the restaurants I'd actually want to go to, and then handling it when the flight gets cancelled. Dealing with insurance claims. Returning things. Rescheduling a doctor's appointment. All the small admin tasks that each take twenty minutes and somehow add up to a whole weekend.

The thing I care about most, though, is that it's reliable enough that I don't have to watch it. The real unlock isn't that it can do a task once in a demo. It's that I can hand something off, go do something else, and come back to it done correctly, or with a clear note about where it got stuck and what it needs from me. That's what a great colleague does, and that's the bar.

r001.rationale: The response describes using an agent for work research and personal tasks such as trip planning and administration, conveying use across distinct areas of life.

r002.rationale: The response says nothing about the pace of AI model improvement or whether it will surprise most people.

astra-6.text:
I’d love for it to take care of the things where I know what outcome I want, but getting there involves a lot of little steps. At work, that could mean taking a question I’m trying to answer, doing the analysis, and bringing back something I can actually use. In my personal life, it might be planning a trip or helping me stay on top of all the administrative stuff that piles up.

And I’d want it to understand my preferences across those different areas, so I don’t have to explain everything from scratch each time. It could figure out what it can handle on its own and when it needs to ask me. That’s the exciting part to me: being able to delegate something and trust that it will follow through.

r001.rationale: The candidate describes one agent helping across work and personal life, including work analysis, trip planning, and administration.

r002.rationale: The candidate does not predict or mention that the pace of AI model improvement will surprise most people.

sol-6.1.text:
I’d love to have an agent that can take care of the coordination across different parts of my life. At work, that might mean helping me research something, write code, and follow through on a project. Outside of work, it could help plan a trip or deal with all the little administrative tasks that pile up.

The exciting part is having something that understands enough context that I don’t have to explain everything from scratch each time. I can tell it what I’m trying to accomplish, and it can figure out the steps, ask me when there’s a meaningful decision, and otherwise just get things done. That would let me spend more time on the things I actually want to be doing.

r001.rationale: The candidate wants one agent to help across work and personal life, with examples including coding at work and trip planning outside work.
